name: polynom
resume: All exports of polynom 1.4-1 are checked, including derivative, prediction, roots, summary, and the plot curve. Coefficient arithmetic stays in Python. Roots are NumPy eigenvalues of the companion matrix. Orthogonal polynomials use NumPy's QR, matching stats::poly. plot draws the curve with Matplotlib. There is no crate.

functions.name: polynomial
functions.done: A coefficient vector becomes a polynomial, lowest degree first.

proof.r:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(polynom))
one <- function() {
  as.character(polynomial(c(1, 2, 1)))
}
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
shown <- enc2utf8(paste(as.character(value), collapse = "|"))
shown <- gsub("\n", " / ", shown, fixed = TRUE)
cat("VALUE ", shown, "\n", sep = "")
cat(sprintf("MS %.17g\n", median(elapsed) * 1000))
proof.python:
from polynom import polynomial, as_character

def one():
    return as_character(polynomial([1, 2, 1]))

import statistics
import time
value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
if isinstance(value, bool):
    shown = "TRUE" if value else "FALSE"
else:
    shown = str(value)
print("VALUE " + shown.replace("\n", " / "))
print(f"MS {statistics.median(elapsed):.17g}")
